docs.title: Google MCP Server
docs.text: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for reading Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Read-only access to Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides via MCP tools
  • 16 tools for comprehensive document access, plus 2 upload tools you turn on with --enable-write
  • Composable architecture built on omniskill
  • Multiple credential options including vault-backed credentials via omnitoken

docs.title: Google Docs Tools
docs.text: Tool Description get_document_metadata Get document metadata (title, word count, element counts) get_document_content Get structured content (headings, paragraphs, images, tables) get_document_text Get all text as a single plain text string get_document_paragraphs Get text organized by paragraphs get_document_suggestions Get text split into original, inserted, and deleted by suggested edits

docs.title: Google Drive Tools
docs.text: Tool Description get_file_comments List a file's comments with quoted text, resolved state, and replies upload_file Upload a local file, optionally converting it (write mode only) update_file Replace a Drive file's content, keeping its ID (write mode only)

docs.title: Google Sheets Tools
docs.text: Tool Description get_spreadsheet_metadata Get spreadsheet metadata (title, sheet count, locale, time zone) list_sheets List all sheets with their properties get_sheet_values Get cell values from a specific range get_sheet_data Get all data from a specific sheet get_multiple_ranges Batch get values from multiple ranges

docs.title: Google Slides Tools
docs.text: Tool Description get_presentation Get presentation metadata (title, slide count, locale, revision ID) list_slides List all slides with titles and element counts get_slide Get slide content and element details by index or object ID get_slide_notes Get speaker notes by slide index or object ID get_presentation_content Get all slides' text and images in one call (ideal for AI)

docs.title: Why Composable?
docs.text:
This server is built on omniskill, making its Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides skills reusable building blocks. You can:

  1. Use standalone - Run mcp-google as a focused Google tools server
  2. Compose with others - Import the skills into a multi-service MCP server combining Google + Slack + Jira + GitHub
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/mcp-google/skills/docs"
    "github.com/plexusone/mcp-google/skills/sheets"
    "github.com/plexusone/mcp-google/skills/slides"
)

// Add to any omniskill-based server
rt.RegisterSkill(docs.New(httpClient))
rt.RegisterSkill(sheets.New(httpClient))
rt.RegisterSkill(slides.New(httpClient))

See Architecture for more details.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install
go install github.com/plexusone/mcp-google/cmd/mcp-google@latest

# Run with Google service account
mcp-google --credentials /path/to/service-account.json

See Getting Started for full setup instructions.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The mcp-google binary can run as an MCP server or call the same Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides tools directly from the command line.

docs.title: Discover Commands
docs.text:
mcp-google --help
mcp-google <command> --help

The CLI is generated with Cobra, so --help is the easiest way to reference the current command list and flags.

docs.title: Server Commands
docs.text: Command Description mcp-google Start the MCP server using stdio mcp-google serve Start the MCP server explicitly (stdio, or HTTP with --http) mcp-google version Print version information

docs.title: HTTP Transport
docs.text: mcp-google serve --http :8080 serves MCP over streamable HTTP instead of stdio, as an OAuth resource server that verifies externally-issued bearer tokens (ID-JAG / Enterprise-Managed Authorization). See HTTP Transport & ID-JAG for the full flag reference, scopes, and audit logging.

docs.title: Google Docs Commands
docs.text:
Command MCP tool get-document-metadata <document-id-or-url> get_document_metadata get-document-content <document-id-or-url> get_document_content get-document-text <document-id-or-url> get_document_text get-document-paragraphs <document-id-or-url> get_document_paragraphs

| get-document-suggestions <document-id-or-url> | get_document_suggestions |

docs.title: Google Drive Commands
docs.text:
Command MCP tool get-file-comments <file-id-or-url> [--include-deleted] get_file_comments upload-file <path> [--name] [--folder-id] [--convert-to doc\|sheet\|slides] upload_file update-file <file-id> <path> [--convert-to doc\|sheet\|slides] update_file

upload-file and update-file change Google data, so they refuse to run unless --enable-write (or MCP_GOOGLE_ENABLE_WRITE=true) is set, and they read local files only from --upload-root. See Google Drive tools.

docs.text:
# Google Docs
mcp-google get-document-metadata https://docs.google.com/document/d/abc123/edit \
  --credentials /path/to/service-account.json

mcp-google get-document-content abc123 \
  --include-metadata \
  --include-images \
  --include-tables \
  --include-headers \
  --include-footers \
  -o pretty

# Google Sheets
mcp-google get-spreadsheet-metadata https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/xyz789/edit \
  --credentials /path/to/service-account.json

mcp-google get-sheet-data xyz789 --sheet-name "Sheet1" -o pretty

mcp-google get-sheet-values xyz789 "A1:D10" --value-format typed -o pretty

# Google Slides
mcp-google get-slide presentation123 --index 0 -o pretty

docs.title: Composability
docs.text: One of the key design goals of Google MCP Server is composability - the ability to combine its skills with others to create multi-service MCP servers.

docs.title: Traditional Approach (Monolithic)
docs.text:
Without composability, you end up with many separate MCP servers:

┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐
│ google-mcp-srv  │  │ slack-mcp-srv   │  │ jira-mcp-srv    │
│   9 tools       │  │   12 tools      │  │   8 tools       │
└─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘
         │                   │                    │
         └───────────┬───────┴────────────────────┘
                     │
              ┌──────▼──────┐
              │  MCP Client │
              │ (3 servers) │
              └─────────────┘

Problems:

  • Multiple processes to manage
  • Multiple connections for the client
  • Harder configuration
  • Resource overhead

docs.title: Composable Approach
docs.text:
With omniskill composability, you can build one unified server:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              work-mcp-server                     │
│  ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌────────┐ │
│  │ slides  │ │  docs   │ │  slack  │ │  jira  │ │
│  └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └────────┘ │
│                    29 tools                      │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                      │
               ┌──────▼──────┐
               │  MCP Client │
               │ (1 server)  │
               └─────────────┘

Benefits:

  • Single process
  • Single connection
  • Unified configuration
  • Lower resource usage

docs.title: Step 1: Import Skills
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/slides"
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/docs"
    // Skills from other repos
    "github.com/example/slack-mcp-skills/skills/messages"
    "github.com/example/jira-mcp-skills/skills/issues"
)

docs.title: Step 2: Create Authentication Clients
docs.text:
Each service needs its own authenticated client:

// Google auth (shared between slides and docs)
googleClient, err := getGoogleHTTPClient(ctx)

// Slack auth
slackClient, err := getSlackHTTPClient(ctx)

// Jira auth
jiraClient, err := getJiraHTTPClient(ctx)

docs.title: Step 3: Initialize Skills
docs.text:
slidesSkill := slides.New(googleClient)
slidesSkill.Init(ctx)

docsSkill := docs.New(googleClient)
docsSkill.Init(ctx)

slackSkill := messages.New(slackClient)
slackSkill.Init(ctx)

jiraSkill := issues.New(jiraClient)
jiraSkill.Init(ctx)

docs.title: Step 4: Register with Runtime
docs.text:
rt := runtime.New(&mcp.Implementation{
    Name:    "work-mcp-server",
    Version: "v1.0.0",
}, nil)

// Register all skills
rt.RegisterSkill(slidesSkill)
rt.RegisterSkill(docsSkill)
rt.RegisterSkill(slackSkill)
rt.RegisterSkill(jiraSkill)

// Serve
rt.ServeStdio(ctx)

docs.title: Complete Example: Multi-Service Server
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/slides"
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/docs"
    "github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
    runtime "github.com/plexusone/omniskill/mcp/server"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Get authenticated clients
    googleClient := getGoogleClient(ctx)

    // Initialize skills
    slidesSkill := slides.New(googleClient)
    if err := slidesSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer slidesSkill.Close()

    docsSkill := docs.New(googleClient)
    if err := docsSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer docsSkill.Close()

    // Create runtime
    rt := runtime.New(&mcp.Implementation{
        Name:    "work-mcp-server",
        Version: "v1.0.0",
    }, nil)

    // Register skills (use prefix to avoid conflicts)
    rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(slidesSkill)  // slides_get_presentation, etc.
    rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(docsSkill)    // docs_get_document_metadata, etc.

    // Run
    if err := rt.ServeStdio(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

docs.title: 1. Use Prefixes When Combining
docs.text:
When combining multiple skills, use RegisterSkillWithPrefix() to avoid tool name conflicts:

rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(slidesSkill)  // slides_*
rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(docsSkill)    // docs_*

docs.title: 2. Share Authentication Where Possible
docs.text:
Google Slides and Docs can share the same authenticated HTTP client:

googleClient := getGoogleHTTPClient(ctx)
slidesSkill := slides.New(googleClient)
docsSkill := docs.New(googleClient)

docs.title: 3. Proper Cleanup
docs.text:
Always defer Close() for each skill:

defer slidesSkill.Close()
defer docsSkill.Close()

docs.title: 4. Handle Initialization Errors
docs.text:
Skills may fail to initialize (network issues, invalid credentials):

if err := slidesSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("Failed to initialize Slides skill: %v", err)
}

docs.title: OmniSkill Integration
docs.text: OmniSkill is a Go framework for building composable MCP servers. Google MCP Server uses omniskill to provide a modular, reusable architecture.

docs.title: What is OmniSkill?
docs.text:
OmniSkill provides:

  • Skill interface: A standard way to package MCP tools
  • Runtime: MCP server with multiple transport options (stdio, HTTP, SSE)
  • Registry: Skill discovery and management
  • Library mode: Direct invocation without MCP protocol overhead

docs.title: Skill Interface
docs.text:
Each Google skill implements the skill.Skill interface:

type Skill interface {
    Name() string                    // Skill identifier
    Description() string             // Human-readable description
    Tools() []Tool                   // List of tools
    Init(ctx context.Context) error  // Initialize before use
    Close() error                    // Cleanup on shutdown
}

docs.title: Slides Skill
docs.text:
package slides

type Skill struct {
    httpClient    *http.Client
    presentations *gslides.PresentationsService
}

func New(httpClient *http.Client) *Skill {
    return &Skill{httpClient: httpClient}
}

func (s *Skill) Name() string { return "slides" }

func (s *Skill) Tools() []skill.Tool {
    return []skill.Tool{
        s.getPresentationTool(),
        s.listSlidesTool(),
        s.getSlideTool(),
        s.getSlideNotesTool(),
        s.getPresentationContentTool(),
    }
}

func (s *Skill) Init(ctx context.Context) error {
    svc, err := gslides.NewService(ctx, option.WithHTTPClient(s.httpClient))
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    s.presentations = gslides.NewPresentationsService(svc)
    return nil
}

docs.title: Docs Skill
docs.text:
package docs

type Skill struct {
    httpClient *http.Client
    documents  *docs.DocumentsService
}

func New(httpClient *http.Client) *Skill {
    return &Skill{httpClient: httpClient}
}

func (s *Skill) Name() string { return "docs" }

func (s *Skill) Tools() []skill.Tool {
    return []skill.Tool{
        s.getDocumentMetadataTool(),
        s.getDocumentContentTool(),
        s.getDocumentTextTool(),
        s.getDocumentParagraphsTool(),
    }
}

docs.title: Tool Definition
docs.text:
Tools use skill.NewTool() for clean definitions:

func (s *Skill) getDocumentMetadataTool() skill.Tool {
    return skill.NewTool(
        "get_document_metadata",
        "Get metadata about a Google Doc document",
        map[string]skill.Parameter{
            "document_id": {
                Type:        "string",
                Description: "The ID or URL of the Google Doc",
                Required:    true,
            },
        },
        func(ctx context.Context, params map[string]any) (any, error) {
            documentID := params["document_id"].(string)
            // ... implementation
            return result, nil
        },
    )
}

docs.title: Runtime Usage
docs.text:
The main server creates an omniskill Runtime and registers skills:

import runtime "github.com/plexusone/omniskill/mcp/server"

// Create runtime
rt := runtime.New(&mcp.Implementation{
    Name:    "mcp-google",
    Version: "v0.4.0",
}, nil)

// Initialize and register skills
slidesSkill := slides.New(httpClient)
slidesSkill.Init(ctx)
rt.RegisterSkill(slidesSkill)

docsSkill := docs.New(httpClient)
docsSkill.Init(ctx)
rt.RegisterSkill(docsSkill)

// Serve via stdio
rt.ServeStdio(ctx)

docs.title: Without Prefix (Default)
docs.text:
Tools are registered with their original names:

rt.RegisterSkill(slidesSkill)
// Tools: get_presentation, list_slides, get_slide, etc.

docs.title: With Prefix
docs.text:
Tools are prefixed with skill name to avoid conflicts:

rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(slidesSkill)
// Tools: slides_get_presentation, slides_list_slides, etc.

This is useful when combining skills that might have tool name conflicts.

docs.title: Benefits of OmniSkill
docs.text:
1. Composability: Skills can be imported into any omniskill-based server
  2. Standardization: Common interface for all skills
  3. Transport flexibility: stdio, HTTP, SSE without code changes
  4. Library mode: Call tools directly without MCP protocol
  5. Registry: Centralized skill discovery

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: Google MCP Server is built on a composable architecture using omniskill, enabling its Google skills to be reused in other MCP servers.

docs.title: 1. Composability First
docs.text:
Rather than being a monolithic MCP server, this project exposes its functionality as skills - modular units that can be:

  • Used standalone in mcp-google
  • Imported into other omniskill-based servers
  • Combined with skills from other services (Slack, Jira, GitHub, etc.)

docs.title: 2. Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
mcp-google/
├── cmd/mcp-google/    # CLI entry point
├── skills/                   # Exportable omniskill modules
│   ├── slides/              # Google Slides skill
│   └── docs/                # Google Docs skill
└── internal/
    └── auth/                # Shared authentication
  • Skills: Contain all business logic, tools, and API interactions
  • CLI: Only handles configuration and skill orchestration
  • Auth: Shared authentication layer using omnitoken

docs.title: 3. Skill Independence
docs.text:
Each skill is self-contained:

  • Has its own Init() lifecycle
  • Manages its own Google API client
  • Defines its own tools
  • Can be registered independently

docs.title: Key Dependencies
docs.text: Package Purpose omniskill Skill framework and MCP runtime omnitoken Token management with vault backends gogoogle Google API utilities oscompat Confined, size-checked file open and capped reader for the upload root goauth Authentication utilities

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Initialization:
  2. CLI parses credentials configuration
  3. omnitoken creates authenticated HTTP client
  4. Skills are initialized with the HTTP client

  5. Skills register with omniskill Runtime

  6. Request Handling:

  7. MCP client sends tool call request
  8. omniskill Runtime routes to appropriate skill
  9. Skill executes tool logic using Google APIs

  10. Response returned via MCP protocol

  11. Shutdown:

  12. Skills Close() called for cleanup
  13. Token manager releases resources

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Google MCP Server supports multiple credential sources for authentication.

docs.title: Option 1: Google Service Account
docs.text: The simplest option - use a standard Google Cloud service account JSON file.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create a service account in Google Cloud Console
  2. Download the JSON credentials file
  3. Share documents with the service account email

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: mcp-google --credentials /path/to/service-account.json

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
{
  "type": "service_account",
  "project_id": "your-project",
  "private_key_id": "key-id",
  "private_key": "<the private_key value from your key file>",
  "client_email": "mcp-server@your-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "client_id": "123456789",
  "auth_uri": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/auth",
  "token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
}

docs.title: Option 2: goauth CredentialsSet
docs.text: Use a goauth CredentialsSet file for managing multiple credentials.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Create a CredentialsSet JSON file with your Google credentials:

{
  "credentials": {
    "myaccount": {
      "type": "gcpsa",
      "gcpsa": {
        "gcpCredentials": {
          "type": "service_account",
          "project_id": "your-project",
          "private_key_id": "key-id",
          "private_key": "<the private_key value from your key file>",
          "client_email": "mcp-server@your-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
          "client_id": "123456789"
        },
        "scopes": [
          "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/presentations.readonly",
          "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents.readonly",
          "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly"
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
mcp-google \
  --goauth-credentials-file /path/to/credentials.json \
  --goauth-credentials-account myaccount

Write mode needs drive.file in the credentials

With a goauth file or a vault, the scopes are the ones configured in the credentials. To use write mode, add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file to them. For a plain service account file, the server adds it for you when --enable-write is set.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Store multiple accounts in one file
  • Pre-configure scopes
  • Consistent credential format across tools

docs.title: HTTP Transport & ID-JAG Authorization
docs.text:
By default mcp-google serves MCP over stdio, with no network exposure. As of v0.4.0 it can also serve over streamable HTTP, secured as a pure OAuth 2.1 resource server that verifies externally-issued bearer tokens (an enterprise IdP, or an ID-JAG delegation-chain token) instead of running its own authorization server.

This is Enterprise-Managed Authorization: your identity provider issues the tokens and owns the trust relationship; mcp-google only verifies them and enforces scope.

docs.title: Enabling HTTP mode
docs.text:
HTTP mode is opt-in. Passing --http (or setting MCP_GOOGLE_HTTP_ADDR) switches the serve command from stdio to streamable HTTP:

mcp-google serve \
  --http :8080 \
  --idjag-issuer https://idp.example.com \
  --idjag-audience https://mcp-google.example.com

--idjag-issuer is required in HTTP mode — it's the authorization server whose tokens will be accepted. --idjag-audience should always be set in production; without it, token audience is not validated and a token minted for a different resource would be accepted.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Environment variable Description --http MCP_GOOGLE_HTTP_ADDR Serve MCP over HTTP on this address (e.g. :8080) instead of stdio --idjag-issuer MCP_GOOGLE_IDJAG_ISSUER Authorization server issuer URL for ID-JAG-derived access tokens (required for HTTP mode) --idjag-audience MCP_GOOGLE_IDJAG_AUDIENCE Expected token audience / resource identifier --idjag-jwks-url MCP_GOOGLE_IDJAG_JWKS_URL Pin the issuer's JWKS endpoint, skipping discovery

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Verified tokens that carry a scope claim are enforced per tool call. Tokens without a scope claim are not gated — the call is allowed, and the identity is still audit-logged.

Authorization uses an explicit map keyed by exact tool name. Every registered tool has exactly one required scope:

Scope Tools docs:read get_document_metadata, get_document_content, get_document_text, get_document_paragraphs, get_document_suggestions sheets:read get_spreadsheet_metadata, list_sheets, get_sheet_values, get_sheet_data, get_multiple_ranges slides:read get_presentation, list_slides, get_slide, get_slide_notes, get_presentation_content drive:read get_file_comments drive:write upload_file, update_file (registered only with --enable-write)

Authorization change in v0.5.0

get_document_suggestions needs docs:read, like the other Docs tools. The new get_file_comments needs drive:read, and the upload tools need drive:write. A deployment that issues scoped tokens must add drive:read and, if it enables write mode, drive:write before callers can use them; until then those calls are denied with a message naming the missing scope. Tokens with no scope claim are not gated, as before. drive:write is advertised in the resource metadata only when write mode is on.

When the token carries a scope claim, a call is denied with an access denied error before it reaches the Google API if:

  • the token's scope claim does not include the tool's required scope (access denied: tool <name> requires scope <scope>), or
  • the tool has no entry in the map (access denied: tool <name> has no scope mapping). Unmapped tools are denied by default rather than allowed.

docs.title: Audit logging
docs.text:
Every tools/call request in HTTP mode is logged via the configured *slog.Logger, including the verified subject, the RFC 8693 act delegation chain (if the token represents a delegated call), the client ID, and the granted scope:

{"msg":"tool_call","tool":"get_document_text","sub":"user@example.com","act":"agent-123","client_id":"mcp-google-client","scope":"docs:read"}

Denied calls are logged separately as tool_call_denied, with the required_scope that was missing, or with reason set to unmapped_tool when the tool has no scope mapping.

docs.title: Google credentials still required
docs.text: ID-JAG / HTTP mode authorizes access to mcp-google's tools. It is independent of how mcp-google itself authenticates to the Google APIs — you still need one of the credential sources described in Credentials (service account, goauth CredentialsSet, or vault-backed).

docs.title: stdio is unaffected
docs.text: If --http / MCP_GOOGLE_HTTP_ADDR is not set, mcp-google behaves exactly as before: it serves over stdio with no token verification, suitable for local use (e.g. Claude Desktop).

docs.title: Create a Google Cloud Service Account
docs.text:
1. Go to the Google Cloud Console
  2. Create a new project or select an existing one
  3. Enable the Google Slides API and Google Docs API:
  4. Go to APIs & Services > Library
  5. Search for "Google Slides API" and enable it

  13. Click on the service account

  15. Add Key > Create new key > JSON
  16. Save the downloaded file securely

Each paragraph and table cell is a block with original, insertion, and deletion segments in document order, and the block's original and accepted text. The Docs API does not report who made a suggestion, so blocks carry no author. See Google Docs tools.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
{ "name": "get_file_comments", "arguments": { "file_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms" } }

Returns { "file_id": ..., "comments": [...] }. Every page is returned, or an error. Author email addresses appear only when Google returns them; treat them as personal data. See Google Drive tools.

docs.title: Write mode
docs.text:
Off by default. Turn it on with a flag or environment variable:

mcp-google serve --enable-write --upload-root ./to-publish
Flag Environment variable Description --enable-write MCP_GOOGLE_ENABLE_WRITE=true Register upload_file and update_file. A service account file also requests the drive.file Google scope. A flag given on the command line, including --enable-write=false, wins over the variable --upload-root MCP_GOOGLE_UPLOAD_ROOT The directory local files are read from (default: the working directory)
  • Narrow scope. Write mode adds only drive.file, which covers just the files the app creates or opens. Without --enable-write the server still requests only read-only Google scopes.
  • Confined paths. A path with .., a rooted or drive path outside the root, or a symbolic link that leaves the root is refused as path_outside_root before anything is sent to Google, the same way on every platform. A symbolic link with an absolute target is refused even when it points back into the root.
  • One open. The file is opened once, through the operating system's confined open, and that handle is checked and streamed to Drive, so a link swapped in at the path afterwards is never followed. Files over 50 MB are refused, and a file that grows past the limit while it is being sent is cut off and refused as file_too_large.
  • Strict arguments. A parameter of the wrong type is refused as invalid_request instead of being read as empty, so a numeric folder_id cannot put the file in the Drive root. File links are accepted only on drive.google.com and docs.google.com.
  • Conversion. convert_to turns .docx, .odt, .txt, or .html into a Google Doc, .csv, .xlsx, or .ods into a Sheet, and .pptx or .odp into Slides.
  • Structured errors. Failures return {"code": ..., "message": ...}: path_outside_root, not_found, permission_denied, unsupported_conversion, file_too_large, invalid_request, write_disabled, or api_error.
  • Audit. Every write call is logged with the caller, tool, file name, and resulting file ID or failure code.

New CLI commands: get-document-suggestions, get-file-comments, upload-file, and update-file. The last two refuse to run without --enable-write.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The Docs, Sheets, and Slides skills no longer build Google API clients or finish API requests; they call gogoogle. A test fails if a skill imports google.golang.org/api/option, builds an API service, or calls .Do().
  • Tool authorization is a literal table keyed by exact tool name instead of substring matching.
  • The server now advertises 16 tools by default and 18 in write mode.

docs.title: Building Multi-Service MCP Servers
docs.text: This guide shows how to combine Google skills with other services to create a unified MCP server.

docs.title: 1. Define Dependencies
docs.text:
// go.mod
module github.com/example/work-mcp-server

require (
    github.com/grokify/mcp-google v0.4.0
    github.com/plexusone/omniskill v0.1.0
    github.com/plexusone/omnitoken v0.1.0
    // Add other skill packages
)

docs.title: 2. Create Skill Providers
docs.text:
Encapsulate skill creation with authentication:

package providers

import (
    "context"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/slides"
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/docs"
    "github.com/plexusone/omniskill/skill"
)

type GoogleProvider struct {
    client      *http.Client
    slidesSkill *slides.Skill
    docsSkill   *docs.Skill
}

func NewGoogleProvider(client *http.Client) *GoogleProvider {
    return &GoogleProvider{client: client}
}

func (p *GoogleProvider) Init(ctx context.Context) error {
    p.slidesSkill = slides.New(p.client)
    if err := p.slidesSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    p.docsSkill = docs.New(p.client)
    if err := p.docsSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    return nil
}

func (p *GoogleProvider) Skills() []skill.Skill {
    return []skill.Skill{p.slidesSkill, p.docsSkill}
}

func (p *GoogleProvider) Close() error {
    _ = p.slidesSkill.Close()
    _ = p.docsSkill.Close()
    return nil
}

docs.title: 3. Configure Credentials
docs.text:
Use omnitoken for unified credential management:

package auth

import (
    "context"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/plexusone/omnitoken"
)

type Credentials struct {
    mgr *omnitoken.TokenManager
}

func NewCredentials(vaultURI string) (*Credentials, error) {
    mgr, err := omnitoken.NewFromVaultURI(vaultURI)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &Credentials{mgr: mgr}, nil
}

func (c *Credentials) GoogleClient(ctx context.Context) (*http.Client, error) {
    return c.mgr.GetClient(ctx, "google")
}

func (c *Credentials) SlackClient(ctx context.Context) (*http.Client, error) {
    return c.mgr.GetClient(ctx, "slack")
}

func (c *Credentials) JiraClient(ctx context.Context) (*http.Client, error) {
    return c.mgr.GetClient(ctx, "jira")
}

func (c *Credentials) Close() error {
    return c.mgr.Close()
}

docs.title: 4. Main Server
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/example/work-mcp-server/auth"
    "github.com/example/work-mcp-server/providers"
    "github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
    runtime "github.com/plexusone/omniskill/mcp/server"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Initialize credentials
    creds, err := auth.NewCredentials(os.Getenv("VAULT_URI"))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer creds.Close()

    // Create runtime
    rt := runtime.New(&mcp.Implementation{
        Name:    "work-mcp-server",
        Version: "v1.0.0",
    }, nil)

    // Initialize Google provider
    googleClient, _ := creds.GoogleClient(ctx)
    googleProvider := providers.NewGoogleProvider(googleClient)
    if err := googleProvider.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer googleProvider.Close()

    // Register Google skills with prefix
    for _, skill := range googleProvider.Skills() {
        rt.RegisterSkillWithPrefix(skill)
    }

    // Add other providers (Slack, Jira, etc.)
    // ...

    // Serve
    if err := rt.ServeStdio(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

docs.title: Using Skills
docs.text: The Google Slides and Docs skills can be imported into any omniskill-based MCP server.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/mcp-google@latest

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/slides"
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/docs"
)

docs.title: Slides Skill
docs.text:
func slides.New(httpClient *http.Client) *slides.Skill

Creates a new Slides skill. The HTTP client must be authenticated with Google OAuth credentials that have the presentations.readonly scope.

docs.title: Docs Skill
docs.text:
func docs.New(httpClient *http.Client) *docs.Skill

Creates a new Docs skill. The HTTP client must be authenticated with Google OAuth credentials that have the documents.readonly scope.

docs.title: Drive Skill
docs.text:
func drive.New(httpClient *http.Client, opts ...drive.Option) *drive.Skill

Creates a new Drive skill. By default it is read-only and provides only get_file_comments, which needs the drive.readonly scope. Pass drive.WithWrite(root) to also provide upload_file and update_file, which read local files only from root and need the drive.file scope. Other options are drive.WithMaxUploadBytes(n) (default 50 MB) and drive.WithLogger(l), which receives the audit record of each write call. In write mode Init fails if root is not an existing directory.

All of the skills go through gogoogle for Google API access; a skill built from an existing gogoogle service is available as NewWithService.

slidesSkill := slides.New(httpClient)
docsSkill := docs.New(httpClient)

    return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize Slides skill: %w", err)
}

if err := docsSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize Docs skill: %w", err)
}

Init() creates the Google API client. It must be called before registering with a runtime.

rt.RegisterSkill(docsSkill)

docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"

    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/slides"
    "github.com/grokify/mcp-google/skills/docs"
    "github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
    "github.com/plexusone/omnitoken"
    runtime "github.com/plexusone/omniskill/mcp/server"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Get authenticated client
    mgr, err := omnitoken.NewFromFile("/path/to/service-account.json")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer mgr.Close()

    httpClient, err := mgr.GetClient(ctx, "google")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Create skills
    slidesSkill := slides.New(httpClient)
    if err := slidesSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer slidesSkill.Close()

    docsSkill := docs.New(httpClient)
    if err := docsSkill.Init(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer docsSkill.Close()

    // Create and configure runtime
    rt := runtime.New(&mcp.Implementation{
        Name:    "my-google-server",
        Version: "v1.0.0",
    }, nil)

    rt.RegisterSkill(slidesSkill)
    rt.RegisterSkill(docsSkill)

    // Run
    if err := rt.ServeStdio(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}

docs.title: PLAN — Review-aware tools — comments, suggestions, and opt-in upload over gogoogle
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-MCPGOOGLE-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/mcp-google Version: 0.1 Status: Draft — pending tech-lead review

Non-normative sequencing of PRD.md and TRD.md; execution state lives in ROADMAP.md.

docs.title: 1. Approach
docs.text:
Authorization comes first. Deny-by-default with an explicit scope map has to be in place before any new tool is registered; otherwise the new tools would bypass policy.

Next, route the Docs skill through gogoogle and bump to the gogoogle release that adds the Drive package and suggestion extraction.

Then add the read tools (suggestions, comments), and only after that the opt-in write tools. Docs and release come last.

docs.title: PRD — Review-aware tools — comments, suggestions, and opt-in upload over gogoogle
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-MCPGOOGLE-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/mcp-google Workflow: pbhq-lite Status: Draft — pending stakeholder review (pbhq-lite gate: after PRD)

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
mcp-google gives AI assistants read-only access to Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. It is a thin MCP wrapper over the gogoogle SDK. When people review a shared document, most of their feedback lives where mcp-google cannot see it:

  1. Comments. Comments come from the Drive API, which mcp-google does not call. An assistant asked "what did reviewers say?" sees none of them.
  2. Suggestions. get_document_text and related tools flatten suggested insertions and deletions into the original text, so proposed edits are indistinguishable from the document itself, and deletions read as if they were still present.
  3. Publishing. An assistant cannot publish a generated file for review. Users upload by hand and convert the file to a native Google format by hand.

There is also a structural issue. The Docs skill calls the Docs API directly (documents.Get) instead of going through gogoogle's docsutil, so it does not benefit from gogoogle improvements.

And there is a security issue. The per-identity tool policy maps tools to scopes by matching substrings of tool names, and it allows any tool that matches no pattern. New tools that do not contain "document", "sheet", or "slide" in their names would bypass scope checks.

Who is affected:

  • AI assistants and agents that run document review loops.
  • Operators who rely on per-identity tool policy.
  • Contributors who expect all Google API logic to live in gogoogle.

Desired state:

  • Assistants can read comments and suggestions in structured form.
  • Assistants can optionally upload files, gated by explicit opt-in and scopes.
  • All Google API calls go through gogoogle.
  • Tool authorization is deny-by-default with an explicit scope per tool.

docs.title: 2.1 Goals
docs.text: ID Goal Success criterion G-1 Thin wrapper No skill calls a Google API client directly; every call goes through a gogoogle package (test: no google.golang.org/api/* service method calls in skills/) G-2 Read suggestions get_document_suggestions returns segments classified original / insertion / deletion with original and accepted text per block G-3 Read comments get_file_comments returns all comments for a Doc, Sheet, or Slides file with quoted anchor text, resolved state, authors, and replies G-4 Optional publishing upload_file and update_file exist only when the server is started with --enable-write, and require the drive:write policy scope over HTTP for tokens that carry a scope claim G-5 Deny-by-default authorization Every registered tool has an explicit required scope; an unmapped tool is denied; a test fails if any tool lacks a mapping G-6 Read-only by default With default flags, the server requests only read-only Google scopes and registers no write tools

docs.title: 2.2 Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Writing comments, replying, resolving, or accepting suggestions.
  • Sharing / permission management.
  • Re-implementing any Google API logic in this repository (it belongs in gogoogle).
  • Converting Markdown or generating documents.

docs.title: 3. User Stories
docs.text:
US-1 — Read what reviewers proposed. As an AI assistant, I want a document's suggestions separated from its text, so that I can summarize or apply proposed edits accurately. Acceptance: get_document_suggestions{document_id} on a fixture returns blocks whose segments match gogoogle's SuggestionContent.

US-2 — Read what reviewers said. As an AI assistant, I want every comment with the text it refers to, so that I can map feedback to sections. Acceptance: get_file_comments{file_id, include_deleted?} returns all pages of comments with quoted text, resolved flag, author display names, and replies.

US-3 — Publish for review (opt-in). As an operator, I want to allow an assistant to upload a generated .docx / .pptx / .csv as a native Google file or update an existing one, so that the review loop needs no manual upload — but only when I explicitly enable it. Acceptance: without --enable-write, the tools are absent from tools/list. With it, upload_file{path, name?, folder_id?, convert_to} returns file ID and link. Over HTTP, a token that carries a scope claim without drive:write is denied and the denial is audit-logged. A token with no scope claim is not gated, as for every other tool.

US-4 — Trust the policy. As an operator, I want new tools to be denied unless explicitly mapped to a scope, so that adding tools never silently widens access. Acceptance: registry test asserts every tool has a mapping; a tool with no mapping is denied at call time.

docs.title: 4. Functional Requirements
docs.text:
• PRD-FR-1 All skills MUST call Google APIs only through gogoogle packages (docsutil, sheetsutil, slidesutil, driveutil).
  • PRD-FR-2 The Docs skill MUST add get_document_suggestions.
  • PRD-FR-3 A new Drive skill MUST add get_file_comments, usable on any file ID.
  • PRD-FR-4 The Drive skill MUST add upload_file and update_file only when --enable-write (or MCP_GOOGLE_ENABLE_WRITE=true) is set. In that mode the server additionally requests the drive.file Google scope.
  • PRD-FR-5 Tool authorization MUST use an explicit tool → scope map:
  • docs:read, sheets:read, slides:read, drive:read for read tools;
  • drive:write for write tools;
  • unmapped tools MUST be denied.
  • PRD-FR-6 Path inputs to write tools MUST be confined to a configured root (--upload-root, default: working directory), rejecting .. escapes and symlinks that leave the root.
  • PRD-FR-7 Documentation (tools reference, configuration, credentials scopes) and release notes MUST cover the new tools, flags, and scopes.

docs.title: 5. Success Metrics (required)
docs.text: Metric Baseline Target Measurement Method Skills calling Google API clients directly 1 (Docs skill) 0 Static test over skills/ Review feedback types readable (text, suggestions, comments) 1 of 3 3 of 3 Tool tests with fixtures Tools without explicit scope mapping All (pattern-based, allow-by-default) 0; unmapped denied Registry test; denial test Write tools registered in default mode 0 0 (unchanged) tools/list test without --enable-write Test coverage of new code 0 % ≥ 80 % go test -cover ./...

docs.title: 6. Out of Scope / Future
docs.text:
• Comment writing / resolution and suggestion acceptance.
  • Permission management.
  • Other Google products (Gmail, Calendar).

docs.title: TRD — Review-aware tools — comments, suggestions, and opt-in upload over gogoogle
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-MCPGOOGLE-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/mcp-google Version: 0.1 Status: Draft

MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD / MAY are used in the RFC 2119 sense.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Purpose. Specify the new tools, the refactor routing all Google API access through gogoogle, the opt-in write mode, and deny-by-default tool authorization.

Scope. This repository's skills, server flags, and authorization only.

References. PRD · PLAN · ROADMAP · gogoogle driveutil/v3, docsutil/v1 (ExtractSuggestionContent) — released in the gogoogle version this work bumps to.

docs.title: 2. Technical Requirements and Traceability
docs.text: TRD ID Requirement Source Verification TRD-001 Skills use only gogoogle packages for Google API calls PRD-FR-1 Static test: no *docs.DocumentsService, *sheets.Service, *slides.Service, or *drive.Service method calls in skills/ TRD-002 get_document_suggestions per §6.1 PRD-FR-2 Tool test with recorded fixture TRD-003 Drive skill with get_file_comments per §6.2 PRD-FR-3 Paged fake-server test TRD-004 Opt-in write tools per §6.3 PRD-FR-4, 6 tools/list tests with and without flag; path-confinement tests TRD-005 Explicit tool → scope map, deny unmapped (§6.4) PRD-FR-5 Registry and denial tests TRD-006 Docs and release notes PRD-FR-7 Docs review; mkdocs build

docs.title: 3. System Invariants
docs.text:
• INV-1 In default mode the server requests only read-only Google scopes and registers no tool that can modify Google data.
  • INV-2 Every registered tool has exactly one required policy scope; a call to a tool without one is denied.
  • INV-3 Skills contain no Google API request logic; they translate MCP inputs and outputs around gogoogle calls.

docs.title: 4. Architecture
docs.text:
MCP client ─► mcp-google (omniskill runtime, stdio or HTTP + ID-JAG policy)
                ├─ docs skill   ─► gogoogle/docsutil
                ├─ sheets skill ─► gogoogle/sheetsutil
                ├─ slides skill ─► gogoogle/slidesutil
                └─ drive skill (new) ─► gogoogle/driveutil  (write tools only with --enable-write)
Component Change skills/docs Use docsutil.Service for all fetches; add get_document_suggestions skills/drive (new) get_file_comments; upload_file, update_file behind opt-in internal/auth Scope set computed from mode: read-only, plus drive.file when write is enabled internal/emauth Explicit tool → scope map; deny unmapped cmd/mcp-google --enable-write, --upload-root flags and env vars; register drive skill

docs.title: 5. State and Lifecycle
docs.text: Not applicable — stateless request/response tools.

docs.title: 6.1 get_document_suggestions
docs.text:
• Input: { "document_id": string }.
  • Output: gogoogle SuggestionContent JSON: document_id, blocks[] with location, segments[] (kind, text, suggestion_ids), original and accepted, plus suggestion_ids.
  • Fetch: docsutil.GetDocumentWithSuggestions(..., "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE").

docs.title: 6.2 get_file_comments
docs.text:
• Input: { "file_id": string, "include_deleted"?: bool }.
  • Output: { "file_id": string, "comments": [Comment] }, where each gogoogle Comment has quoted_text, resolved, author, replies[], and timestamps. The list is a field of an object because MCP structured tool results are objects.
  • Scope: works for Docs, Sheets, and Slides files.

docs.title: 6.3 Write tools (opt-in)
docs.text:
Tool Input Output upload_file { path, name?, folder_id?, convert_to: "doc"\|"sheet"\|"slides"\|"" } gogoogle File JSON (id, name, mime_type, web_view_link) update_file { file_id, path, convert_to? } gogoogle File JSON

Registration. These tools are registered only when --enable-write is set or MCP_GOOGLE_ENABLE_WRITE=true.

Path handling. path is resolved against --upload-root. A request is rejected when:

  • the cleaned path escapes the root;
  • the path or any parent is a symlink resolving outside the root;
  • the file is larger than 50 MB.

Audit. Every write call is audit-logged with the identity, tool, file name, and resulting file ID.

docs.title: 6.4 Authorization map
docs.text:
Tool Required policy scope get_document_* (metadata, content, text, paragraphs, suggestions) docs:read get_spreadsheet_metadata, list_sheets, get_sheet_values, get_sheet_data, get_multiple_ranges sheets:read get_presentation*, list_slides, get_slide* slides:read get_file_comments drive:read upload_file, update_file drive:write

The map is a literal Go table keyed by exact tool name, replacing substring matching. When a token carries no scope claim, behavior stays as today (stdio and tokens without scopes are not gated). When a scope claim is present, unmapped tools are denied.

docs.title: 6.5 Errors
docs.text:
• Tool errors return MCP isError: true with JSON { code, message }. Codes:
  • not_found
  • permission_denied
  • unsupported_conversion
  • path_outside_root
  • write_disabled
  • file_too_large
  • invalid_request
  • api_error
  • Scope denials keep the existing denial format and are audit-logged.

docs.title: 7. Data Design
docs.text: No persistence. Tool outputs reuse gogoogle JSON types unchanged, so the wrapper adds no schema of its own.

docs.title: 8. Operational Guarantees
docs.text: Category Requirement Measurement Applicability Performance Comment listing makes one API call per page Fake-server request count Applicable Auditability Every write call and every denial is audit-logged Log-capture tests Applicable Availability, throughput Not applicable — per-process tool server — —

docs.title: 9. Security and Privacy
docs.text:
• Least privilege. Default mode requests only the read-only scopes (INV-1). Write mode adds only drive.file, never full drive.
  • Deny-by-default. Explicit per-tool scopes (INV-2) close the current gap where unmapped tools are allowed.
  • Filesystem confinement. Upload paths are confined to --upload-root.
  • Personal data. Comment author emails are passed through only when the API returns them. The docs advise treating them as personal data.
  • Not applicable. Encryption at rest (no storage); in transit, Google client TLS and the existing HTTP transport settings apply.

docs.title: 10. Compatibility and Migration
docs.text:
• Applicable. Existing tool names, inputs, and outputs are unchanged.
  • Authorization change. Deny-unmapped applies only to tokens that carry a scope claim. Deployments that issue scoped tokens must add drive:read and/or drive:write to use the new tools. This is noted in the release notes.

docs.title: 11. Dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Version Purpose github.com/grokify/gogoogle v0.13.0 or later (adds driveutil/v3, ExtractSuggestionContent) Google API SDK github.com/plexusone/omniskill current (v0.12.0) Skill runtime github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk current MCP

docs.title: 12. Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Tool tests. Each tool is tested against gogoogle fake servers (via option.WithEndpoint).
  • Registry test. Asserts INV-2 (every tool has a scope mapping).
  • Static test. Asserts INV-3 (no direct Google API calls in skills).
  • Write mode. tools/list snapshots with and without --enable-write.
  • Path confinement. Tests cover .., absolute paths outside the root, and symlinks.

docs.title: 13. Deployment
docs.text:
• Release. Ship as a minor release (v0.5.0) after the gogoogle release is tagged.
  • Rollout. Write mode is off by default.
  • Rollback. Pin v0.4.0.

docs.title: 14. Alternatives Considered
docs.text: Alternative Why rejected Implement Drive calls directly in a new skill Duplicates SDK logic; other Go programs and the gogoogle CLI need the same functions Keep substring-based scope mapping and add "file" / "comment" patterns Still allow-by-default; fragile as tool names grow Always register write tools, relying on Google scopes to fail Exposes write intent to every client and widens requested OAuth scopes by default

docs.title: 15. Risks and Open Questions
docs.text:
ID Risk / Question Mitigation R-1 Scoped-token deployments lose access to new tools until policies are updated Release notes; clear denial messages naming the missing scope R-2 Service accounts cannot see files not shared with them Documented in setup guide (share the folder with the service account)

No open question blocks implementation.

docs.title: Google Docs Tools
docs.text:
URL Support

All Google Docs tools accept either the document ID or the full URL, including URLs with query strings and anchors like: 

https://docs.google.com/document/d/abc123/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.xyz

docs.title: get_document_metadata
docs.text: Get metadata about a Google Doc document.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Doc

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description title string Document title document_id string Document ID revision_id string Current revision ID word_count integer Approximate word count char_count integer Character count image_count integer Number of images table_count integer Number of tables header_count integer Number of headers footer_count integer Number of footers

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_document_metadata",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
  }
}

docs.title: get_document_content
docs.text: Get the full structured content of a document including headings, paragraphs, and optionally images and tables.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Doc include_images boolean No Include image information (default: false) include_tables boolean No Include table content (default: false) include_headers boolean No Include document headers (default: false) include_footers boolean No Include document footers (default: false) include_metadata boolean No Include document metadata and content counts (default: false)

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description title string Document title metadata object Document metadata and content counts (if requested) metadata.document_id string Document ID metadata.revision_id string Current revision ID metadata.word_count integer Approximate word count metadata.char_count integer Character count metadata.image_count integer Number of images metadata.table_count integer Number of tables metadata.header_count integer Number of headers metadata.footer_count integer Number of footers sections array Array of content sections sections[].type string Section type ("heading", "paragraph") sections[].level integer Heading level (1-6, for headings only) sections[].text string Section text content sections[].style_id string Style identifier (e.g., "HEADING_1") images array Array of images (if requested) images[].object_id string Image element ID images[].content_uri string Direct URL to image images[].source_uri string Original source URL images[].title string Image title images[].description string Image description tables array Array of tables (if requested) tables[].rows integer Number of rows tables[].columns integer Number of columns tables[].cells array 2D array of cell text content headers array Array of header text (if requested) footers array Array of footer text (if requested)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_document_content",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "https://docs.google.com/document/d/abc123/edit",
    "include_images": true,
    "include_tables": true,
    "include_metadata": true
  }
}

docs.title: get_document_text
docs.text: Get all text content from a document as a single plain text string.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Doc

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description title string Document title text string Full document text

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_document_text",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
  }
}

Best for Simple Text Extraction

Use this when you just need the raw text content without structure.

docs.title: get_document_suggestions
docs.text: Get a document's text split by pending suggested edits. Each paragraph and table cell is a block, with segments of original, inserted, and deleted text in document order, plus the block's original text and its text as if every suggestion were accepted.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Doc

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Field Type Description document_id string The document ID blocks array One block per paragraph and table cell, in document order, including blocks with no suggestions suggestion_ids array The distinct suggestion IDs, in document order

Each block has:

Field Type Description location string body/p/<n> for a paragraph, or body/table/<n>/r/<row>/c/<col> for a table cell segments array Segments with kind (original, insertion, or deletion), text, and suggestion_ids original string The original and deleted text: the block before any suggestion accepted string The original and inserted text: the block with every suggestion accepted

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_document_suggestions",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
  }
}

Authors are not available

The Google Docs API does not say who made a suggestion, so blocks carry no author. Comments do: use get_file_comments.

docs.title: get_document_paragraphs
docs.text: Get text organized by paragraphs.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description document_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Doc

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description title string Document title paragraphs array Array of paragraph text strings

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_document_paragraphs",
  "arguments": {
    "document_id": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
  }
}

Best for Paragraph-Level Processing

Use this when you need to process text paragraph by paragraph, such as for summarization or analysis tasks.

docs.title: Google Drive Tools
docs.text:
Drive tools read the comments on any file and, only when you turn on write mode, upload files and replace their content. They work on Docs, Sheets, and Slides files as well as any other Drive file.

Tool Mode Scope Purpose get_file_comments default drive:read Comments with quoted text, resolved state, and replies upload_file write mode only drive:write Upload a local file, optionally converting it to a Google file update_file write mode only drive:write Replace a Drive file's content, keeping its ID

Read-only by default

In default mode the server registers no tool that can change Google data and requests only read-only Google scopes. upload_file and update_file do not appear in tools/list until the server is started with --enable-write.

docs.title: get_file_comments
docs.text: List the comments on a Drive file, with the text each is anchored to, whether it is resolved, and its replies. Every page of results is returned, or an error: never a partial list.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The file ID, or a Drive, Docs, Sheets, or Slides link on drive.google.com or docs.google.com include_deleted boolean No Include deleted comments (default: false)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Field Type Description file_id string The file ID that was read comments array The comments, in the order Drive returns them

Each comment has:

Field Type Description id string Comment ID content string The comment text quoted_text string The text in the file the comment is anchored to anchor string The anchor, when the API provides one author object display_name, and email_address only when the API returns it created_time, modified_time string RFC 3339 timestamps resolved boolean Whether the thread is resolved deleted boolean Whether the comment is deleted replies array Replies, each with id, content, action (resolve or reopen when the reply did that), author, and created_time

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_file_comments",
  "arguments": {
    "file_id": "https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms/edit"
  }
}

Treat author email addresses as personal data

Email addresses appear only when Google returns them. Do not pass them on to systems that do not need them.

Suggested edits are not comments

Use get_document_suggestions for the suggested edits in a Google Doc. Together with the document text and these comments, that covers all three kinds of review feedback.

docs.title: Write mode
docs.text: Write mode lets an agent publish a document for review and keep it up to date without a manual upload. It is off unless you ask for it.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
mcp-google serve --enable-write --upload-root ./to-publish
Flag Environment variable Description --enable-write MCP_GOOGLE_ENABLE_WRITE=true Register upload_file and update_file. A service account file also requests the drive.file Google scope. A flag given on the command line, including --enable-write=false, wins over the variable --upload-root MCP_GOOGLE_UPLOAD_ROOT The directory the tools may read local files from (default: the working directory)

The upload root must exist when the server starts. The same flags apply to the upload-file and update-file CLI commands, which refuse to run without --enable-write.

In write mode the server requests the drive.file Google scope in addition to the read-only scopes. drive.file covers only the files the app creates or opens, never the whole Drive. If your credentials come from a goauth file or a vault, their configured scopes must include drive.file; for a service account file the server adds it for you.

docs.title: upload_file
docs.text:
Upload a local file, optionally converting it to a Google Doc, Sheet, or Slides file.

Parameter Type Required Description path string Yes Path of the local file, relative to the upload root name string No Name for the Drive file (default: the file name, without its extension when converting) folder_id string No ID of the Drive folder to put the file in convert_to string No doc, sheet, or slides. Omit to store the file unchanged

Output is the new file: id, name, mime_type, web_view_link, head_revision_id, and modified_time.

{
  "name": "upload_file",
  "arguments": {
    "path": "review/packet.docx",
    "convert_to": "doc",
    "folder_id": "1AbCdEfGh"
  }
}

docs.title: update_file
docs.text:
Replace the content of an existing Drive file with a local file. The file ID, link, sharing, and comments are kept, so reviewers keep working in the same document.

Parameter Type Required Description file_id string Yes The ID or link of the Drive file, on drive.google.com or docs.google.com path string Yes Path of the local file, relative to the upload root convert_to string No doc, sheet, or slides. Omit to store the file unchanged

Which files can be updated

With the drive.file scope, update_file can change only files that the server's credentials created, or that a person opened with the app. A file that was merely shared with a service account is outside that scope, and Drive refuses the update as permission_denied or not_found. Publish the file with upload_file first, and update the copy the server created. The server does not ask for the broader drive scope, which would reach the whole Drive.

docs.title: Conversions
docs.text:
convert_to Accepted extensions Result doc .docx, .odt, .txt, .html Google Doc sheet .csv, .xlsx, .ods Google Sheet slides .pptx, .odp Google Slides file

An extension that does not match the target is refused as unsupported_conversion.

docs.title: What a path may be
docs.text:
A path is confined to the upload root. These are refused with path_outside_root, the same way on every platform, before anything is sent to Google:

  • a .. element, with / or \ as the separator;
  • a rooted or drive-qualified path that is not inside the root, such as /etc/passwd, C:x, or a UNC path;
  • a path that leads outside the root through a symbolic link, in any element of the path.

The path must name a regular file no larger than 50 MB.

The file is opened once

The server opens the file once, inside the upload root, and the operating system refuses a symbolic link that leads out of the root at the moment of the open. The file type and size are checked on that open handle, and the handle itself is streamed to Drive, so the path is not opened a second time. A link swapped in at the path after the open is never followed, and a file that grows while it is being sent is cut off at the limit and refused as file_too_large.

A symbolic link with an absolute target is refused even when it points back inside the root, because the operating system's confined open does not follow absolute links. A link with a relative target that stays inside the root is followed.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A failed write returns an error result whose text is JSON, {"code": "...", "message": "..."}:

Code Meaning path_outside_root The path leaves the upload root not_found No such local file, or Drive says the file does not exist or is not shared with the credentials permission_denied Drive refused the request. Check the credentials' access and that drive.file was granted unsupported_conversion convert_to is not doc, sheet, or slides, or the extension does not match file_too_large The file is over the 50 MB limit, or grew past it while it was being sent invalid_request A missing or malformed argument, or a path that is not a regular file write_disabled A write was requested with write mode off (the CLI commands) api_error Any other Drive failure

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Every write call is logged, whether it succeeds or fails, with who made it, which tool, the file name, the Drive file an update targets, and the resulting file ID or the failure code:

{"level":"INFO","msg":"write_call","tool":"upload_file","name":"packet.docx","sub":"user@example.com","client_id":"client-1","scope":"drive:write","file_id":"1AbCdEf"}
{"level":"WARN","msg":"write_call_failed","tool":"upload_file","name":"x","sub":"user@example.com","code":"path_outside_root"}
{"level":"WARN","msg":"write_call_failed","tool":"update_file","name":"packet.docx","target":"1AbCdEf","sub":"user@example.com","code":"not_found"}

Over stdio there is no verified identity, so sub is local. File contents, credentials, and paths on the server's disk are never logged.

docs.title: Service accounts
docs.text: A service account sees only the files shared with it, and the files it creates are owned by it. Share the target folder with the service account's email address before uploading into it.

docs.title: Tools Overview
docs.text: Google MCP Server provides 16 tools for reading Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive comments, and 2 more that upload files when you turn on write mode.

docs.title: Tool Categories
docs.text: Category Tools Description Google Docs 5 tools Read documents, content, paragraphs, and suggested edits Google Drive 1 tool, plus 2 in write mode Read file comments; upload and update files Google Sheets 5 tools Read spreadsheets, sheets, and cell values Google Slides 5 tools Read presentations, slides, and speaker notes

docs.title: Google Docs
docs.text: Tool Purpose get_document_metadata Document metadata (title, word count) get_document_content Structured content with optional images/tables get_document_text Plain text extraction get_document_paragraphs Text organized by paragraphs get_document_suggestions Text split into original, inserted, and deleted by suggested edits

docs.title: Google Drive
docs.text: Tool Purpose get_file_comments Comments on any file, with quoted text, resolved state, and replies upload_file Upload a local file, optionally converting it (write mode only) update_file Replace a Drive file's content, keeping its ID (write mode only)

docs.title: Google Sheets
docs.text: Tool Purpose get_spreadsheet_metadata Spreadsheet metadata (title, sheet count) list_sheets List all sheets with properties get_sheet_values Cell values from a specific range get_sheet_data All data from a specific sheet get_multiple_ranges Batch get values from multiple ranges

docs.title: Google Slides
docs.text: Tool Purpose get_presentation Presentation metadata (title, slide count) list_slides List all slides with titles get_slide Single slide content and elements get_slide_notes Speaker notes for a slide get_presentation_content All content in one call (ideal for AI)

docs.title: AI Analysis of Entire Document
docs.text:
For AI analysis, use the bulk retrieval tools:

  • Docs: get_document_content with all include flags
  • Sheets: get_sheet_data with include_metadata: true
  • Slides: get_presentation_content with include_notes: true

docs.title: Targeted Retrieval
docs.text:
For specific content:

  • Docs: Use get_document_paragraphs for structured text
  • Sheets: Use get_sheet_values for specific ranges
  • Slides: Use list_slides then get_slide for specific slides

docs.title: Reviewing a Document
docs.text:
To read all the feedback on a Google Doc:

  • Text: get_document_text or get_document_paragraphs
  • Suggested edits: get_document_suggestions
  • Comments: get_file_comments

docs.title: Metadata Only
docs.text:
For quick metadata checks:

  • Docs: get_document_metadata
  • Sheets: get_spreadsheet_metadata
  • Slides: get_presentation

docs.title: Google Sheets Tools
docs.text:
URL Support

All Google Sheets tools accept either the spreadsheet ID or the full URL, including URLs with query strings and fragments like: 

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=0

  "name": "get_spreadsheet_metadata",

docs.title: Input

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description spreadsheet_id string Spreadsheet ID title string Spreadsheet title sheets array Array of sheet information sheets[].index integer Zero-based sheet index sheets[].sheet_id integer Sheet GID sheets[].title string Sheet name sheets[].sheet_type string Sheet type (GRID, CHART, etc.) sheets[].hidden boolean Whether the sheet is hidden sheets[].row_count integer Number of rows sheets[].column_count integer Number of columns sheets[].frozen_row_count integer Number of frozen rows (if any) sheets[].frozen_column_count integer Number of frozen columns (if any)

docs.title: get_sheet_values
docs.text: Get cell values from a specific range.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description spreadsheet_id string Yes The ID or URL of the Google Sheets spreadsheet range string Yes A1 notation range (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:D10', 'A:D', 'A1:D10') sheet_index integer No Zero-based sheet index. Used when range doesn't include sheet name. sheet_name string No Sheet name. Used when range doesn't include sheet name. Mutually exclusive with sheet_index. value_format string No Output format: 'formatted' (default), 'typed', 'raw'

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Field Type Description spreadsheet_id string Spreadsheet ID range string Resolved range with sheet name values array 2D array of cell values (format depends on value_format)

docs.title: Value Formats
docs.text:
formatted (default): Display values as strings

{
  "values": [
    ["Name", "Date", "Amount"],
    ["Alice", "Jan 15, 2024", "$1,234.56"]
  ]
}

typed: Values with type information

{
  "values": [
    [
      {"type": "string", "formatted_value": "Name"},
      {"type": "string", "formatted_value": "Date"},
      {"type": "string", "formatted_value": "Amount"}
    ],
